why: A method of an argument's class comes before MATLAB's function of the name (MATLAB doc 'Function Precedence Order', 'Method Invocation'): `disp(g)` calls `@gadget/disp.m` and `disp(k)` calls `Gizmo`'s `disp`. In `plain.m`, `noclass()` is a function, so `n` is a struct and `disp(n)` is MATLAB's own: no edge, and no row either (project rule, step 15 round 3: such a call is kept, dormant, only while a class of its callee's name exists, any package and any case, or while a plain call of the built-in's name would be kept; neither holds here) (the step 15 review's probe, extended).
